title: DISCO: Mitigating Bias in Deep Learning with Conditional Distance Correlation
claim: Dataset bias arises from a small set of canonical causal structures, each linking a bias variable to input and label differently.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, small causal graphs with captions beneath
description: Three side-by-side causal DAG panels on a white background, each captioned below: (a) Confounder, (b) Collider, (c) Mediator. Every panel has circular nodes for input X and label Y, with an arrow from Y to X (the anti-causal direction). In (a), a bias node B_c sits below and points to both X and Y. In (b), a bias node B_col points to X and to a grey-shaded node S. Y also points to S, so S is a collider that is conditioned on. In (c), Y points to a bias node B_M, which then points to X, making B_M a mediator. The grey fill on S is the only color. The eye goes first to the shaded collider node and then across the three graph shapes.
caption: Canonical causal structures that induce dataset bias. Grey nodes indicate latent conditioning.
abstract: Dataset bias often leads deep learning models to exploit spurious correlations instead of task-relevant signals. We introduce the Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM), a unifying causal framework that characterizes bias mechanisms and yields a conditional independence criterion for causal stability. Building on this theory, we propose DISCO$_m$ and sDISCO, efficient and scalable estimators of conditional distance correlation that enable independence regularization in gradient-based models. Across six diverse datasets, our methods consistently outperform or are competitive in existing observed bias mitigation approaches, while requiring fewer hyperparameters and scaling seamlessly to multi-bias scenarios. This work bridges causal theory and practical deep learning, providing both a principled foundation and effective tools for robust prediction. Source Code: https://github.com/yakamoz5/DISCO.
